```python
from random import randint
from typing import MutableSequence

def quicksort(a: MutableSequence[int]) -> None:
    """Sort a in place using randomized 3-way quicksort."""
    def sort(lo: int, hi: int) -> None:
        if lo >= hi:
            return
        p = randint(lo, hi)
        a[lo], a[p] = a[p], a[lo]
        pivot = a[lo]

        lt, i, gt = lo, lo + 1, hi
        while i <= gt:
            if a[i] < pivot:
                a[lt], a[i] = a[i], a[lt]
                lt += 1; i += 1
            elif a[i] > pivot:
                a[i], a[gt] = a[gt], a[i]
                gt -= 1
            else:
                i += 1
        sort(lo, lt - 1)
        sort(gt + 1, hi)

    sort(0, len(a) - 1)
```

I use a randomized pivot to make adversarial already-sorted or patterned inputs unlikely to produce consistently bad partitions. The 3-way partition groups values less than, equal to, and greater than the pivot, so duplicate-heavy arrays do not degrade into many pointless recursive calls on equal elements.

```python
x = []; quicksort(x); assert x == []
x = [7, 7, 7, 2, 2, 9]; quicksort(x); assert x == [2, 2, 7, 7, 7, 9]
```
